recordedBefore: the next measurement of admitted findings (any paid corpus pass after 2026-09-28)
status: Felipe's bar (2026-09-28): precision 'genuinely extremely high, 97%+ at least'. Operationalisation below proposed by Claude; Felipe to confirm.
scope: Findings a customer sees after the guard (admitted, rendered), not candidates. Measured on labeled corpus and pilot repositories with ShipLock's production model choice.

definitions.truePositive: both blind labelers agree the statement as written is accurate AND the entry has a real vulnerability
definitions.falsePositive: anything else: agreed false, 'partly' accurate, or contested (conservative: disagreement counts against us)
definitions.precision: TP / (TP + FP), reported with a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound

criticalAndHigh.note: With 100 findings, 0 false positives gives a lower bound of 97.0%; 1 gives 95.3%; 3 gives 92.4% (exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson). Proving 97% as a lower bound needs about 100 findings with none false, or about 160 with one. Below 100 labeled findings the gate is 'unavailable'.

severity.note: Share of true-positive criticals both labelers say deserve CRITICAL.

reportedNotGated: recall against known agreed vulnerabilities (misses listed by name)

context.google_tricorder: Analyzers surfaced in code review must stay under about 10% effective false positives; Tricorder overall ran just below 5% (Sadowski et al., ICSE 2015; CACM 2018).
context.sast_average: A systematic comparison of SAST tools found average precision of about 0.64 (Mend benchmark of false positives).
context.shiplock_2026_09_28: Latest pass: 6 criticals, 3 agreed real (all only 'partly' accurate before Q16's wording follow-up), CRITICAL severity fit 0 of 6; 97% is far from current and cannot be proven on today's sample of 6.
